title: 10 Steps to Great Customer Service
blurb: The ten habits of great service, from a prompt greeting to a warm farewell, and how to recover when things go wrong.
siteNotes: Greeting and farewell wording the venue prefers, if it has a house style
Where menu and daily specials information is kept so staff can brush up before service
legalNotes: From BHB-10MT-22. Service good practice; no regulation is involved.
The ten steps as listed in the trainer: greet, connect, welcome, anticipate, know your stuff, be attentive, stay positive, stay tidy, recover well, send them off happy.

cards.title: 10 Steps to Great Customer Service
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- greet every guest promptly and warmly
- anticipate needs without hovering
- recover well and send guests off happy

cards.title: Noticed, welcome, looked after
cards.body: Great service turns a first-time visitor into a regular and a good wedding into one guests talk about for years. It is not about being posh or stuffy. It is about making every guest feel noticed, welcome and genuinely looked after from arrival to leaving.

cards.title: The basics, done consistently
cards.body:
Smile and greet people promptly, make eye contact and be genuinely warm rather than going through the motions. When you are rushed, a quick "I'll be right with you" tells a waiting guest they have been seen.
> Being ignored is what really annoys people.

items.title: Welcome
items.text: Make them feel seen, even when busy

cards.title: Be switched on
cards.body: Know your menu so you can answer questions and recommend dishes. Anticipate needs before you are asked. Be attentive without hovering.

items.title: Anticipate
items.text: Top up water, clear plates before asked

cards.title: Positive and tidy
cards.body: Handle every request positively and keep your areas clean and tidy.

left.title: Say
items: Keep your area clean and tidy

cards.title: Recover and send off
cards.body: When something goes wrong, deal with it gracefully rather than getting flustered or defensive. Finish with a warm farewell and a genuine invitation to come back.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Smile and greet promptly. Being ignored annoys guests most.
- When busy, say "I'll be right with you".
- Know your menu and anticipate needs, without hovering.
- Say "let me sort that for you", never "that's not my section".
- Recover calmly, then finish with a warm farewell and an invitation back.

cards.q: What is the first step of great service when a guest arrives?
options: Offer them the wine list
Ask if they have booked
Smile and greet them promptly
Show them to a table
cards.why: It starts with the basics: smile and greet people promptly.

cards.q: Great service means making every guest feel noticed and looked after.
cards.why: Service is about making every guest feel noticed, welcome and genuinely looked after.

cards.q: You're rushed and a guest is waiting. Best thing to do?
options: Ignore them until you are free
Tell them you are too busy
Ask them to wait at the bar
Say "I'll be right with you"
cards.why: A quick "I'll be right with you" tells a guest they have been seen. Being ignored is what annoys people.

cards.q: You should know your menu so you can answer questions and recommend dishes.
cards.why: Knowing your menu lets you answer questions and make recommendations.

options: Warm and welcoming
Friendly and polite
Prompt and helpful
Hovering over them
cards.why: Attentive without hovering: be there when needed, but do not crowd the guest.

cards.q: "That's not my section" is a great way to handle a guest request.
cards.why: "Let me sort that for you" beats "that's not my section" every time.

cards.q: What does "anticipate needs" mean in service?
options: Wait to be asked, then act fast
Offer the most expensive option first
Spotting and meeting needs before you are asked
Check back every two minutes
cards.why: Anticipating means topping up water or clearing plates before the guest has to ask.

cards.q: Being ignored is one of the things that annoys guests most.
cards.why: Being ignored is what really annoys people, which is why a quick acknowledgement matters.

options: A cold, quick goodbye at the door
Silence as they head for the door
Just the bill and a nod goodbye
A warm farewell and an invitation back
cards.why: Finish with a warm farewell and a genuine invitation to come back.

cards.q: Which of these shows genuine warmth when greeting a guest?
options: A quick nod while you carry on typing
A fast recital of the specials
A smile, eye contact and a real welcome
Asking them to wait to be seated
cards.why: Be genuinely warm rather than going through the motions: smile, eye contact and a real welcome.
